description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy across three distinct metrics: overall accuracy, change in accuracy (Δ Accuracy), and initial accuracy. The x-axis represents “Initial Confidence,” ranging from 0.81 to 0.99 in a linear scale, with tick labels displayed at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis represents “Accuracy,” scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0. The blue line, marked with circles and error bars, depicts overall accuracy, starting at approximately 1.0, dipping slightly to about 0.92 around 0.87, and then rising again to a final value of approximately 0.98 near 0.99. The orange line, marked with diamonds and error bars, represents Δ Accuracy, beginning near 0.45, declining to a low of about 0.10 near 0.87, and then fluctuating slightly before ending near 0.05. The green line, marked with squares and error bars, shows Initial Accuracy, starting at approximately 0.55, rising steadily to about 0.95 near the end of the x-axis.
